Nakhon Ratchasima: a 16-route bus network and 172 existing routes
se: The meeting considered the status of existing routes and operating rights, and how to arrange a public transport network in Nakhon Ratchasima province. OTP proposed a network of 16 bus routes, about 525 kilometres in all, with about 750 bus stops, covering about 200,000 people or 47 per cent of the study area, using 251 electric buses (EV): 170 in the first phase and 81 in the second. The Department of Land Transport reported 172 existing category 1 and 4 routes, 119 with an operator and 53 without. The new network overlaps existing routes by about 40–86 per cent, which may affect existing operators' rights; improving existing routes can be done faster than setting new ones. The meeting suggested separating re-routing from the switch to EV buses, setting clear overlap criteria, choosing pilot routes with the whole network in mind, ring and feeder routes, no more than 1 change of bus per trip, updating the law so local governments clearly have power to run bus services, reviewing fares against real costs and what people can pay, indirect income such as advertising on buses, and GPS, real-time bus tracking apps and a common ticket. The meeting took note and asked OTP and the Department of Land Transport to prepare more information, such as overlap criteria, a review of the passenger model and whether there are enough EV buses.
